title: Policy Safety Net Canonicalizer and Validator for Region/Tier Routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the policy engine intake to produce a canonical, validated representation of smart routing rules (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants). Current problem: multiple legacy schema variations and permissive parsing lead to silent policy mismatches in Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket implements a canonicalizer + safety-net validator that (1) rejects unsafe or ambiguous rules at intake with actionable errors, (2) emits a deterministic canonical AST used by the dispatcher and policy simulator, and (3) provides a migration shim for older configs to opt into automated fixes with audit logging. The goal is to reduce incidents caused by mis-declared fallbacks and unintended cross-region routing while preserving gradual migration for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Policy intake rejects invalid field combinations (e.g., region-tier pair incompatible with customer region constraints) and returns a user-friendly error code and link to docs
A canonical AST format is defined and documented; both the policy compiler and routing dispatcher consume it without per-deployment conditional parsing
Migration shim can automatically rewrite 95% of legacy rule patterns to canonical form; rewrites are logged and exposed in console diffs

Unit and integration tests cover region selection heuristics, tier fallback sequencing, and fallback-to-variant substitution logic with edge-case scenarios (cascading fallbacks, weighted-region mixes)
Performance overhead of canonicalization validation in hosted API path <= 3ms p50 and <= 10ms p95 for typical rule-size (<= 16 predicates)
Security review completed for config parsing and audit logging (KMS/HSM implications in Private deployments)
technical_notes: Introduce canonical AST (flat list of ordered rules + normalized conditions + explicit fallback chains). Representation uses arrays of atomic predicates; avoid nested polymorphic blobs.

Validation rules include schema conformance, constraint logic (no circular fallbacks), region/tier compatibility matrix check, and capacity-affinity semantic checks (e.g., 'prefer-tier:gpu' requires corresponding capacity config)
Implement a two-stage ingest: fast syntactic parse (no enforcement) then synchronous semantic validation that runs background heuristics for suggested rewrites
Provide a 'lint' mode in CLI/Console that surfaces non-blocking recommendations (e.g., ambiguous 'region: nearest' when customer has geo-block) and a 'strict' mode for enterprise tenants
Rules will be versioned (policy_v1 -> policy_v2) with a small compatibility shim in the control plane; onboarding includes a dry-run transform API endpoint
migration_plan: Phase 1: Schema spec & canonical AST design (docs + examples) — deliver design doc and unit spec
Phase 2: Implement parser + canonicalizer library with extensive unit tests; publish internal npm/py package and bump runtime consumer
Phase 3: Add opt-in migration shim that rewrites legacy configs and stores original in audit_log; enable dry-run API for customers
Phase 4: Canary rollout for 5% of hosted traffic with dashboard metrics to detect routing deltas and latencies
Phase 5: Escalation rules and automatic rollback hooks if rollback spike or customer-impacting deltas detected
Phase 6: Gradually flip strict validation on for new config writes after 6 weeks of monitoring and customer outreach
rollout_steps: Merge canonicalizer with feature flag 'policy_canonicalizer' off by default
Run offline migration tool against internal config corpus and sample customer configs; create diff reports
Enable dry-run endpoint and invite 3-5 early adopter customers to opt-in for rewrite feedback
Enable feature flag for internal infra and dedicated staging clusters; monitor p50/p95 canonicalization latency
Canary enable for hosted routing path (5% traffic) with continuous A/B compare of route decisions
If stable, ramp to 25% then 100% while notifying support and solutions teams
qa_tests: Unit: parser fuzz harness with mutated legacy schemas; expect deterministic canonical output or clear parse error
Integration: end-to-end routing simulation comparing old and new dispatcher outputs over historical request traces
Performance: microbench canonicalizer latency under concurrency (1000 qps) and memory profile checks
Security: malformed policy inputs should never perform IO; parser must run in sandboxed context; audit log must mask secrets
Chaos: simulate regional capacity loss and ensure fallback model variants follow declared weights and do not route to unauthorized regions
